sections.h2: What to sort out first in West Milford
sections.html:
West Milford is a sprawling, lake-dotted township in northern Passaic County, and a sale here turns on three things: a fire-safety certificate from the township, the assessment calendar kept by the Passaic County Board of Taxation, and a deed filed with the county clerk in Paterson. Nearly nine in ten houses have the owner living in them, so most buyers will be families moving in, with investors a smaller group.

The sections below cover the local market, what its lakes and watershed mean for a listing, the alarm certificate, the tax calendar and the filing that ends the process.

At 75.93 square miles of land, West Milford is the biggest municipality in Passaic County. It has 25,216 residents, and workers face a long drive, with a commute near 40 minutes.

About 95 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, so few houses change hands in a given year. A lakefront cottage and a hilltop colonial can sit far apart in value, so ask an agent for sold prices on your own road rather than rely on the township middle figure.

The township describes itself as many small towns, with the township center, Hewitt, Newfoundland and Oak Ridge as the four main communities. After the war, the cottages around the lakes gradually became year-round houses. Greenwood Lake runs about nine miles and crosses into New York, and smaller waters such as Upper Greenwood Lake, Wonder Lake and Lake Lockover have their own clusters of homes.

  • Large tracts around the Pequannock watershed belong to the City of Newark, so a view of that land will not be built over.
  • The 2004 Highlands Water Protection and Planning Act puts West Milford in the Highlands preservation area, which brings extra state rules. Check with the township before telling a buyer that an addition or a new lot is possible.
  • Jungle Habitat, a safari park open from 1972 to 1976, passed to the state in 1988 and is now a mountain biking destination that outdoor-minded buyers like.

Route 23 carries most through traffic, with County Routes 511 and 513 close behind. The township counted 198.30 miles of roadway, of which 163.20 miles belonged to the township and the rest to the county or the state, so find out which agency maintains the road in front of your house. NJ Transit buses 194 and 196 run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown, and the township operates two limited local bus routes.

Families will want the elementary school for your street named in the listing, so get that from the school district office.

A house for one or two households cannot change owners until the Fire Marshal's office certifies that its smoke and CO alarms pass inspection. The state rule is N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3, and skipping it can mean a fine of up to $2,500. Inspections are booked for Wednesdays, so start early.

  • Fees on the township's February 2025 sheet run $55 for a request made more than 10 business days ahead, $100 for four to ten days, and $165 inside four business days. A second visit costs $50.
  • Alarms must carry a UL listing and be under 10 years old, and plain battery units must use sealed 10-year batteries.
  • Any home with a fuel-burning appliance, fireplace, wood stove or attached garage needs a CO alarm.
  • No certificate is issued unless house numbers at least four inches tall can be seen from the street.
  • A solar array, generator or battery backup calls for a label by the electric panel and meter that reads "CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER."
  • A fire extinguisher is no longer part of the requirement for one- and two-family homes.

The certificate lasts six months and does not transfer to a later owner. The Fire Prevention Bureau is at 13 Edgar Drive, and its phone is 973-728-2840.

Walk the house with the list before you book. Check the age printed on each alarm, confirm the house number is visible from the road, and look at any solar or generator equipment for the required label. Fixing these items costs little, and a failed visit means a second fee and a later closing date.

The assessor mails a postcard to every owner on February 1 listing the assessment for the current tax year. If you think it is too high, a petition goes to the Passaic County Board of Taxation by April 1, and forms are available from the township assessor at 973-728-2793. Added or omitted assessments, which appear when new construction is added to the roll partway through a year, have a separate December 1 deadline.

The county board sits at 930 Riverview Drive, Suite 250, in Totowa. When you sell, ask the township tax collector for your current balance and any sewer charge so the title company can build an exact payoff.

sections.h2: Deed filing and the state transfer fee
sections.html:
The Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division, at 401 Grand Street, Room 113, in Paterson, records West Milford deeds. A deed must show a "Prepared by" line, the tax block and lot, the price and a return address. The office asks for an official cover sheet, and without one it adds $20 per document.

The seller also pays the state realty transfer fee, a tiered charge that rises with the price and is paid by trust account check. Your closing attorney will compute it from the state schedule, and the county adds a $5 homelessness trust fund charge per document.

The lakes, long drives and low turnover here affect which route makes sense, and each one still needs the alarm certificate and a clean title.

  • An agent listing helps most when the house is far from Route 23 or on a lake road, because the wide buyer pool includes commuters who will trade drive time for space.
  • A sale on your own can work with a neighbor or relative as buyer, though you take on pricing, disclosures and the contract.
  • A cash purchase suits an inherited house, a camp-style cottage needing work or an owner who has already moved away.

Compare offers by the amount left after the certificate, taxes, state fee and repairs, not by the headline price.

faqs.q: Is an alarm certificate required to sell in West Milford?
faqs.a: Yes, for houses of one or two units. The Fire Marshal's office issues it, the township sheet lists fees of $55, $100 or $165 depending on how near closing you apply, and it expires after six months.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Milford house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The alarm certificate looks at alarms, house numbers and a few related items, not the overall condition of the house. A mortgage lender may still demand repairs, while a cash buyer can take it in its current condition.

faqs.q: By what date must a West Milford assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: Every April 1, with the Passaic County Board of Taxation, once the February postcard has arrived. Appeals about added or omitted assessments are due December 1.

faqs.q: Which office records a West Milford deed?
faqs.a: The Passaic County Clerk's Registry Division in Paterson. The closing attorney or title agent files it and sends the seller's transfer fee at the same time.

faqs.q: Does the Highlands Act affect a West Milford sale?
faqs.a: It can shape what a buyer may build. West Milford lies in the Highlands preservation area, so additions and new lots face added state rules, while an existing house sells like any other.
